question: What scaffolding do Tengyu Ma and SallyAnn DeLucia each argue is necessary around current LLM systems, and what underlying limitation motivates it in each case?
expected_answer: Tengyu Ma argues that today's RAG systems require many 'tricks' on top of the model layer — parsing strategies, chunking strategies, recursive search, contextual chunks, graph RAG — because embeddings, rerankers, and large language models are not yet perfect. SallyAnn DeLucia argues that LLM agents require explicit planning scaffolding: Alyx has three to-do tools (write, update, read), four states (pending, completed, blocked, in progress), and a 'finish gate' that blocks task completion until every to-do is done. Both motivate their scaffolding by an LLM limitation — imperfect retrieval/generation for Tengyu, and the inability of simple prompts or a finish tool to keep the agent on task for SallyAnn.
expected_claims: Tengyu Ma argues that current RAG systems require many 'tricks' on top of the model layer, including parsing strategies, chunking strategies, recursive search, contextual chunks, and graph RAG.
Tengyu Ma motivates these tricks by saying that embeddings, rerankers, and large language models are not yet perfect.

SallyAnn DeLucia argues that Alyx needs explicit planning scaffolding: three to-do tools (write, update, read), four states (pending, completed, blocked, in progress), and a 'finish gate' that blocks completion until every to-do is done.
SallyAnn DeLucia motivates this scaffolding by saying that using a simple finish tool or prompts alone was not enough for Alyx to accomplish complex tasks.
